heroHeadline: Carney Pivots to Europe: Canada Pushes for Full Strategic Partnership With EU as US Tariff Standoff Continues
heroSubtitle: In the most optimistic public signal from either government since the Aug 21 talks collapse, Trump said Sept 12 in Dublin that a US-Canada deal could come 'fairly soon' once Ottawa addresses US grievances over dairy market access, repeating a disputed claim that Canada charges American farmers tariffs as high as 400%. PM Carney responded Sept 14, telling Bloomberg 'I welcome the president's comments' and that he remains open to a deal 'that respects our sovereignty, respects obviously the U.S. sovereignty,' while cautioning 'there's not a pride thing' standing in the way. Carney made the remarks while opening his Canada Investment Summit in Toronto, drawing roughly 300 CEOs managing more than $120 trillion in combined assets to pitch Canada's energy, critical-mineral and manufacturing sectors as an alternative to US-bound capital; he was set to head to Europe afterward to address the European Parliament. No new formal bilateral negotiating session has been confirmed as resumed, and Canada's Sept 8 retaliatory tariffs and the US's Sept 8 import bans on Canadian dairy, alcohol and motor vehicles remain in effect.
